intent: Give the new ~/untools Flutter app a launcher icon from the shared family (charcoal field + accent glyph), so it does not ship the stock Flutter beach icon, and whitelist its package in phone_focus_mode's config.
scope: phone_focus_mode/config.sh — add com.kuhy.untools to the productive-apps whitelist
Non-goal: no change to render/style/generate; the shared palette and safe-box rules are untouched
changes: Added _DECISION_TREE: one node branching into two, drawn as hollow rings (r=78) so the 72px stroke leaves visible negative space at icon size. A two-level, seven-node version was tried first and rejected — the generator's safe-box check flagged it as overflowing by ~170x162px, and at 48dp the doubled connectors closed into a solid mass. Branch spread was then narrowed from 324/700 to 346/678 to clear a residual 44px horizontal overflow.
Registered the untools AppIcon (accent #B8862E, glyph decision-tree, linux=False because the desktop build is the web build in a Chrome --app window, so there is no GTK app to hand a hicolor PNG to).

Added com.kuhy.untools to config.sh's user-requested productive apps. Note this is source-of-truth only: the current Pixel 6a (23181JEGR08034) is not rooted, has no /data/local/tmp/focus_mode directory and no running daemon, so nothing was pushed to the device and no app is at risk of being killed there. Kept for the rooted BL9000 phone / any future redeploy.

verification.evidence: 44 passed; app_icons at 100% (apps.py 24/24, glyphs.py 28/28, cli.py 60/60, generate.py 41/41). The repo-wide 5.35% total is the monorepo bar applied to a single-subpackage run, not a regression from this change.
wrote 6 asset files to /home/kuhy/untools/assets/icon; regenerated Android mipmaps; no safe-box warning on the final geometry.

verification.command: visual inspection of assets/icon/icon.png and icon_foreground.png
verification.evidence: Symmetric tree, three hollow rings holding their negative space, charcoal #211D1B field with #B8862E glyph — consistent with the rest of the family.
Installed and launched; app alive after 4s (pid present), confirming no focus-mode interference on this device.

risks: The glyph reads as a generic org-chart/hierarchy at very small sizes; it is distinguished from the family's other glyphs by shape, and no other app uses a node-and-edge motif.

config.sh now lists a package that is not enforced on the current device. Harmless, but a reader could infer the whitelist is live here when it is not — the comment in this evidence file and the commit message state otherwise.
rollback: Revert the three files; delete ~/untools/assets/icon and the android mipmaps it regenerated.
After rollback, re-run the app_icons test suite (44 tests) and confirm the registry test still passes with the untools entry removed.
